jobs.title: 3D Printer Technician
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Physical Intelligence is bringing general-purpose AI into the physical world. We are a group of engineers, scientists, roboticists, and company builders developing foundation models and learning algorithms to power the robots of today and the physically-actuated devices of the future.


THE TEAM

The Robotics Technician Team works closely with PI's fleet operations and engineering teams to maintain the robotic platforms that power our AI research. The team is collaborative, fast-moving, and deeply technical, and this role is a direct partner to the technicians and engineers who depend on printed parts to keep robots running.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The 3D Printer Technician owns additive manufacturing for the Robotics Technician Team. You will run and maintain the team's 3D printers across multiple locations, manage the print request queue, set and hold print standards, and keep a stocked supply of printed spare parts at each site so technicians never wait on a print. You will work directly with hardware engineers, prototype technicians, and robot service technicians at every location.


IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Print Queue & Request Intake
   
   - Own the print request queue in Linear. Every request carries the part, revision, quantity, material, requester, and need-by date.
   
   - Prioritize the queue with robot downtime first and production builds second.
   
   - Confirm each request points at a released Onshape model before printing, and route undocumented parts back to the requester.
   
   - Post daily queue status: printing now, next up, blocked, and expected ready times.

 - Printer Operation & Maintenance
   
   - Run every printer the team owns, at every location: slicing, bed preparation, starts, monitoring, part removal, and failed print recovery.
   
   - Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for every printer at every location (nozzles, beds, belts, extruders, firmware, calibration) and log every PM.
   
   - Diagnose and repair printer failures at any location, and keep a spares kit at each site so a down printer is back in service the same day.
   
   - Move between locations on a set cadence for PMs, repairs, and calibration, and respond to printer outages wherever they happen.
   
   - Track and report printer uptime by location monthly.

 - Materials & Post-Processing
   
   - Own filament and resin inventory: stock levels, dry storage, reorder points, and purchasing within set limits.
   
   - Maintain one standard print profile per material and part family, versioned with the part.
   
   - Post-process every part to its drawing (supports, heat set inserts, hardware, finishing) and inspect with calipers before release.
   
   - Stock printed spares at every site to set minimums for high-turn parts so technicians pull from a bin, not the queue.

 - Documentation & Standards
   
   - Maintain a printed parts library: part number, revision, material, profile, print time, where it is used, and stock at each site.
   
   - Track print volume and failure rate by part and by printer, and report monthly on what is trending the wrong way.
   
   - Own the printer access list and train technicians who keep print access on the standard workflow and profiles.
   
   - Follow the team's ticket closeout and handoff guide on every print ticket.


WHAT WE HOPE YOU'LL BRING

 - Additive Manufacturing Experience: 2+ years running FDM printers in a production, lab, or service environment, including maintenance and repair, not just operation.

 - Slicer Fluency: Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, Cura, or equivalent. Able to build and tune a profile from scratch and explain why each setting is where it is.

 - CAD Literacy: Able to open a CAD model, check a dimension, repair a mesh, and adjust a tolerance for print.

 - Mechanical Skillset: Comfortable with calipers, heat set inserts, threaded hardware, and inspecting parts to a drawing.

 - Multi-Site Coverage: Comfortable splitting time between locations and owning printer uptime at sites you are not at every day.

 - Detail Oriented: Holds parts to a standard and tracks what went wrong when a print fails.

 - Strong Communication: Clear written queue updates and failure reports, and direct cross-functional communication with hardware engineers, prototype technicians, and robot service technicians.


BONUS POINTS

 - SLA or SLS printing experience

 - Onshape experience

 - Experience using Linear ticketing system

jobs.description:
About Us: 

Homebound is on a mission to make it possible for anyone, anywhere, to build a home using technology. Created by an experienced team of construction, real estate, design, and technology experts, Homebound is transforming the residential construction industry by improving the costly and inefficient process of building a home. 

We’ve created an entirely new way to build homes with technology powering every stage from start to finish to provide a seamless experience for our customers. Homeowners across the country can choose where they want to live, select a home plan that’s perfect for them, then personalize and buy it, all online. Homebound has raised $150M in capital from leading venture capitalists like Google, Khosla, Thrive Ventures, and we’re scaling quickly in places like Texas, Colorado and Florida. Homebound is seeking an experienced Construction Superintendent to join our Tampa team and lead field operations for our single-family home projects. As a Superintendent, you’ll be responsible for managing the entire construction process—from mobilization to delivery—with an uncompromising focus on safety and quality. Delivering homes on schedule and on budget is important, but secondary to building exceptional homes, safely.

What You'll Do:

jobs.title: Hardware Engineer
jobs.description:
HARDWARE ENGINEER

We’re looking for a Hardware Engineer to develop electronic products from concept through production. You’ll own circuit design, PCB development, prototype bring-up, and hardware validation to deliver reliable, production-ready systems. You will work alongside our cofounder / CTO who earned 7 patents for electronics. This role is best suited for a skilled engineer who wants to move fast in a small team. 




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own hardware development from requirements and architecture through schematic capture, PCB layout, validation, and production release.

 - Select components, define footprints, and manage bills of materials with attention to performance, availability, cost, and lifecycle.

 - Design analog and digital circuits, power supplies, sensor interfaces, communication interfaces (I²C, SPI, UART, USB, Ethernet, etc.), and microcontroller/processor subsystems.

 - Perform circuit simulation and engineering analysis to evaluate power, signal integrity, timing, and thermal performance.

 - Bring up and debug prototypes using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, and other lab equipment.

 - Develop validation plans, characterize hardware performance, and resolve issues identified during testing.

 - Collaborate with firmware, mechanical, test, and manufacturing engineers throughout the development cycle.

 - Prepare design documentation and lead design reviews, supporting Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Test (DFT), and cost reduction.

 - Support EMC/EMI, environmental, safety, and regulatory testing as products mature.

 - Troubleshoot production issues and implement design improvements to increase reliability and manufacturing yield.
   
   


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent practical experience.

 - 3+ years of hands-on electronic circuit and PCB design experience.

 - Proficiency with schematic capture and PCB design tools such as Altium, Cadence, or KiCad.

 - Solid understanding of analog and digital electronics, power supply design, and signal- and power-integrity fundamentals.

 - Experience designing microcontroller or processor-based systems and common communication interfaces.

 - Hands-on experience bringing up and debugging custom hardware using standard lab instrumentation.

 - Ability to translate system requirements into practical designs and clearly document engineering decisions.
   
   


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering.

 - Experience with SPICE, signal- and power-integrity analysis, or electromagnetic and thermal simulation tools such as Ansys HFSS, SIwave, Icepak, or CST.

 - Experience designing hardware for robotics, autonomous systems, industrial, aerospace, or defense applications.

 - Familiarity with DFM, DFT, component sourcing, and manufacturing processes.

 - Python or other scripting experience for test automation, hardware characterization, or data analysis.

 - Experience with EMC/EMI troubleshooting and environmental or regulatory compliance testing.

jobs.title: Robot Service Technician Assistant - Part Time Evenings
jobs.description:
About the Team

Since 2017, Avride has been building expertise in autonomous technologies to create solutions that address current needs and anticipate future demands.  We are a U.S.-based autonomous vehicle startup headquartered in Austin, Texas with additional R&D hubs around the world. Our company develops and operates both autonomous cars and delivery robots that share technologies and mutually benefit from each other’s advancements — a unique approach in the industry.

About the Role

Avride is preparing to launch a fleet of autonomous delivery robots at multiple campuses across the U.S. and we are hiring a motivated, entry-level Robot Service Technician Assistant to support this exciting deployment. In this role, you will support the daily operations, maintenance, and preparations of our delivery robots. This part-time and weekend-based role is the perfect starting point for individuals looking to build a career in robotics and electro-mechanical assembly. You will ensure our fleet is ready for deployment while learning foundational skills needed to advance in our rapidly growing industry.

This position is employed through our staffing partner and offers weekly pay.

Schedule:

Part-Time Evening Schedule – Ideal for College Students!

This position offers a flexible evening schedule that's ideal for current college students looking to gain hands-on technical experience while balancing their classes.

• Schedule: 4–5 evenings per week, most shifts will include some weekend nights (Fri, Sat and/or Sun)

• Hours: 2–3 hours per shift, scheduled between 7:00 PM and 12:00 AM

What You’ll Do

• Prepare robots for the shift: Ensure all hardware and software are ready for daily deployment.

• Put robots/batteries on chargers for the night: Manage power cycles to ensure maximum fleet readiness.

• Clean robots: Maintain physical appearance and protect sensitive external hardware.

• Perform mechanical repairs: Assist with and execute basic repairs on the robot fleet.

• Perform service campaigns: Help implement widespread hardware or software updates across the fleet.

• Assist remote support coordinators: Act as the hands-on field contact for the remote tracking team.

• Perform calibrations and wheel alignment: Ensure sensors and chassis components are properly tuned for safe navigation.

• Keep workshop clean and tidy: Maintain a safe, organized, and efficient workspace for the entire technical team.

What You’ll Need

• Comfortable working in varied field environments.

• Ability to lift and move items over 50 pounds safely.

• Strong attention to detail and a logical approach to problem-solving.

• Team-oriented mindset with strong communication and collaboration skills.

Nice to Have

• General computer literacy.

• Introductory background or interest in electric vehicle (EV) service, automotive repair, or electronics.

Candidates are required to be authorized to work in the U.S. The employer is not offering relocation, sponsorship, and remote work options are not available.

Avride is an equal opportunity employer and committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants and employees with disabilities to ensure they have equal access to employment opportunities. jobs.description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?




YOUR MISSION

Finance teams lose hours every week chasing approvals, re-keying data, and reconciling records across systems that don’t talk to each other. As a member of UiPath’s product marketing team, you’ll bring our agentic solutions for the Office of the CFO to market, focusing on the source-to-pay and order-to-cash functions. These solutions orchestrate work across the ERP, procurement, and receivables systems customers already run. Drawing on your knowledge of how finance organizations buy and what they’re measured on, you’ll own positioning, launches, and sales enablement that speak to finance leaders in their own terms.




WHAT YOU’LL DO AT UIPATH

 - Lead go-to-market strategy and launch planning for source-to-pay (invoice processing, procurement, and supplier communications) and order-to-cash (collections and cash application), working with the field marketing and sales teams that bring it to market.

 - Define positioning and messaging for the full CFO buying center, from AP, AR, and procurement leaders to controllers and the CFO, presenting UiPath as the layer that orchestrates work across their existing systems rather than replacing them.

 - Build the sales story and the tools to tell it: pitch decks, battlecards, ROI calculators, demo narratives, objection handling, and sales training.

 - Recruit customer advocates and turn their results into proof points tied to finance KPIs such as DSO, cost per invoice, and on-contract spend.

 - Run buyer research, including personas, buying journeys, and win/loss analysis, and share what you learn with product management to shape the roadmap.

 - Develop the messaging, content, and audience insight behind campaigns across demand generation, field, and partner channels, and support analyst relations.

 - 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 10+ years in B2B marketing, consulting, or product development, ideally including SaaS product marketing for finance, procurement, or order-to-cash software.

 - Deep knowledge of source-to-pay and order-to-cash processes and the finance leaders who own them. Experience in finance operations, shared services, or finance advisory is a strong plus.

 - Working knowledge of enterprise SaaS, GenAI, agentic AI, and automation, including how they integrate with ERP and other systems of record, and the ability to explain them in terms of business outcomes.

jobs.title: RTL Design Engineer, Networking / NoC
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an RTL Design Engineer to help design and develop next-generation AI accelerator silicon. In this role, you'll work across architecture, microarchitecture, and RTL implementation, translating complex system and performance requirements into efficient, scalable hardware designs.

You'll collaborate closely with silicon architects, hardware and software engineers, verification, and physical design teams to co-design hardware solutions optimized for demanding AI workloads. This is a hands-on engineering role with opportunities to influence architectural decisions, drive microarchitecture development, and own RTL design from early concept through implementation and integration.

We're particularly interested in engineers with experience in Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect architectures, or high-performance data movement, though the role encompasses broader RTL design and hardware co-design challenges.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement high-performance RTL for next-generation AI accelerator silicon, from microarchitecture definition through implementation and integration.

 - Collaborate with architecture and software teams to translate system-level requirements into efficient hardware microarchitectures.

 - Drive hardware/software co-design efforts to optimize performance, power, area, and scalability for AI workloads.

 - Develop and optimize RTL for complex datapaths, control logic, interconnects, and other critical silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and microarchitectural tradeoffs across bandwidth, latency, throughput, and resource utilization.

 - Partner with design verification and formal verification teams to ensure functional correctness, develop verification strategies, and debug complex design issues.

 - Work closely with physical design teams to optimize RTL for synthesis, timing closure, power, and area.

 - Contribute to architecture reviews, design specifications, and cross-functional discussions to influence future silicon designs.

 - Support block-level and SoC-level integration, debugging, and performance optimization.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong hands-on experience with ASIC RTL design and microarchitecture development using SystemVerilog or Verilog.

 - Have experience designing and implementing complex digital hardware blocks, from architecture and specification through RTL development and verification.

 - Understand hardware architecture and microarchitecture tradeoffs, including performance, power, area, latency, and throughput.

 - Have experience collaborating across architecture, software, verification, and physical design teams to develop optimized hardware solutions.

 - Can reason about complex hardware systems, identify performance bottlenecks, and translate architectural requirements into efficient RTL implementations.

 - Have experience with synthesis, timing closure, and physical implementation considerations.

 - Enjoy working on ambiguous, technically challenging problems and taking ownership of designs from concept through integration.

 - Bring experience with Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect fabrics, packet-based architectures, or high-bandwidth data movement systems.

 - Experience with AI accelerators, high-performance computing, or hardware/software co-design is a plus.

jobs.title: Associate Scientist, LNP Analytics
jobs.description:
About Stylus Medicine:

Stylus Medicine is developing transformative in vivo genetic medicines to unlock cures. Stylus combines engineered recombinases with non-viral delivery to specifically encode therapeutics. The company’s approach is versatile and modular, with potential therapeutic application across oncology, autoimmune, genetic diseases, and beyond.

About the Role:

Stylus Medicine is seeking an intellectually curious and collaborative Associate Scientist to join our analytical development team and aid in the development of characterization techniques for lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to be used for in vivo delivery of genome engineering material. This role will be responsible for both providing analytical support to the delivery team as well as driving the development of novel analytical techniques. Reporting to the Principal Scientist, LNP Analytics, this individual will play an integral role in advancing transformative in vivo genetic medicines.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities:

• Leverage expertise in lipid chemistry, LNP formulation and analytical characterization to advance novel gene editing modalities across different stages of drug development

• Develop methods such as BLA, CBQCA, DLS, , UPLC, HPLC-CAD, IP-RP HPLC, LC-MS/MS, CGE, BLI/SPR, ELISA and ddPCR/qPCR to screen and support optimal LNP formulations for in vitro and in vivo applications

• Author standard operating procedures, study plans, reports, and present findings to project teams and leadership

• Work in close collaboration with the cross-functional teams to support in vitro and in vivo experiments assessing biodistribution, safety and efficacy of LNP formulations

• Foster external collaborations and stay abreast of emerging trends and innovations in LNP technology, proposing new approaches to enhance the company’s delivery platforms, as appropriate

Qualifications & Skills:

• Undergraduate or master’s degree in biochemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or a related field

• 2-4 years of industry/academic experience focusing on LNP characterization

• Prior experience with characterization of targeted nanoparticles is strongly preferred

• Strong foundation in lipid chemistry, formulation development, and analytical techniques

• Familiarity with gene editing modalities or nucleic acid delivery (e.g. CRISPR/Cas, base editing, mRNA, DNA) is a plus

• Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced, innovative environment

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to meet project deliverables and timelines

• Demonstrated ability to work independently, multitask effectively, and maintain strong written documentation

Pay Range: $105,000-$115,000

jobs.title: Mission Software Engineering Intern (Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

Every flight test day at REGENT generates a flood of vehicle data, and the faster that data turns into engineering answers, the faster our Seaglider programs move toward production. As a Mission Software Engineering Intern, you'll own a bounded project of your own in test, ground systems, or vehicle health monitoring — something like telemetry prioritization for constrained radio links, ingest and replay tooling, or a fault-detection prototype — built and verified against recorded data and bench setups. You'll also help build the downstream data path for our test infrastructure effort: the schemas, ingest pipelines, and quick-look analysis tools that turn raw telemetry into something engineers can actually use.

You'll sit within Mission Software Engineering, a team working across navigation and route software, perception and autonomy interfaces, vehicle deployment tooling, and the test and ground systems that support all of it. This team believes rigor should scale with criticality, and you'll see that principle in action as your tooling supports real test campaigns and crew-facing, vehicle-health data. 

If you're a graduate student who wants hands-on ownership of real engineering problems - not a side project, but work the team will actually rely on - we'd love to meet you.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own a Scoped Project: You'll take ownership of one focused project in test and ground systems or vehicle health monitoring, such as telemetry prioritization for constrained links, ingest and replay tooling, or a fault-detection prototype.

 - Build the Downstream Data Path: You'll contribute to our test infrastructure effort, helping design telemetry schemas and build ingest, replay, and quick-look analysis tooling that engineers depend on after a test day.

 - Work Against Real Vehicle Data: You'll build and verify your project against recorded data and bench setups, learning how the vehicle's publish/subscribe data model moves information across topics, QoS, and schemas.

 - Test for the Hard Cases: You'll write automated tests that cover the scenarios that actually break systems in the field, including stale, missing, delayed, and malformed data.

 - Get Close to Flight Test: You may support live test campaigns and work with crew-facing and vehicle health data, giving you a front-row seat to how rigor is matched to criticality across the vehicle.

 - Collaborate Across Vehicle Programs: You'll work alongside engineers supporting Paladin, Viceroy, and Squire, picking up context on navigation, perception interfaces, and deployment tooling along the way.

 - Document and Present Your Work: You'll walk the team through your design decisions and findings, leaving behind documentation they can reuse and build on well after your internship ends.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Graduate-Level Foundation: You're currently enrolled in an M.S. or PhD program in computer science, software engineering, robotics, ECE, aerospace, or a related field.

 - Fluency in Python and C++: You're strong in Python and/or modern C++ (17 or later) and comfortable building and debugging in a Linux environment from day one.

 - Rock-Solid CS Fundamentals: You have a genuine command of software design, data structures, concurrency, and automated testing, and you know how to apply that rigor to real systems.

 - A Distributed Systems Mindset: You're familiar with event-driven or publish/subscribe systems, message passing, and networking, and you think naturally in terms of topics and data flow.

 - Hands-On With Pub/Sub Middleware: Experience with DDS, ROS 2, MQTT, or similar middleware is a strong plus and will shorten your ramp-up on the vehicle's data model.

 - Telemetry and Visualization Chops: Experience with data logging, time-series pipelines, or building dashboards will serve you well, since most project areas center on exactly this kind of tooling.

 - Simulation and Replay Experience: Prior work with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop setups, or log replay tooling for robotic or vehicle software is a bonus, though we'll teach you our specific setup.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

jobs.title: Business Development Manager, San Francisco
jobs.description:
Life Space Digital is reshaping the out-of-home media landscape through the deployment of digital screens in high-traffic office, multifamily, and retail environments. Our platform delivers content-rich experiences and targeted advertising directly to building occupants and visitors — starting in elevators, lobbies, and shopping center concourses. Backed by an experienced leadership team and aggressive growth targets, we are scaling across key U.S. markets with a focus on speed, precision, and long-term value for our partners.


We are seeking a Business Development Manager to support growth across key markets by building strategic partnerships with property owners, developers, and operators in the office and multifamily space. You will help develop territory strategies, build relationships with key stakeholders, and manage deals from initial outreach through close. This role is suited for a business development professional with strong real estate fluency, experience building partnerships, and the ability to operate in a fast-moving, scaling environment.



We partner directly with leading property owners to modernize buildings, elevate tenant experience, and unlock new revenue opportunities through digital media. At Life Space Digital, we combine high design with smart technology to redefine what people expect from everyday spaces.

 

Your Focus in the Sales Funnel:

 - Own market development and partner outreach within assigned territories

 - Drive prospect engagement and support multi-site deal execution

 - Collaborate with leadership to support go-to-market strategies

 

What you'll get to do in this role:

 - Own market development and partner outreach within assigned territories

 - Set and execute territory strategies to drive partner acquisition across key markets

 - Build and nurture relationships with property groups, asset managers, and portfolio owners

 - Manage a high-volume pipeline with support from internal marketing and operations teams

 - Close long-term agreements that create strategic value and unlock revenue opportunities

 - Partner cross-functionally with internal teams to support smooth handoffs and implementation

 - Share market intelligence on landlord priorities, competitive trends, and partner needs

 

Who you are:

 - 3-5 years of experience in business development, strategic partnerships, commercial real estate sales, or a related field

 - Experience developing relationships with property owners, operators, asset managers, or real estate decision-makers

 - Proven ability to manage a pipeline, lead outreach, and close partnership or sales agreements

 - Familiarity with office, multifamily, retail, or commercial real estate markets such as New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, or Chicago

 - Strong communication skills with the ability to tailor value propositions to different stakeholders

 - Comfortable operating in early-stage and scaling environments with high performance expectations

 - Experience using a CRM; previous experience with HubSpot is preferred

 

Life Space Digital offers a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees, including:

 - Healthcare: Medical coverage to keep you and your family healthy (employer covered premiums up to 100%)

 - Dental: Comprehensive dental plan

 - Vision: Vision coverage for eye care and eyewear

 - Talkspace Therapy Package: Access to mental health support

 - Commuter Benefits: Assistance for in-office employees’ commuting costs

 - Short-Term Disability: Financial protection in case of temporary disability

 - 401(k): Retirement savings plan with company match

 - Paid Time Off (PTO): Generous leave for vacation, personal time, and holidays

 

The base pay range for this position is $80,000-$100,000 with an uncapped commission structure. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, candidate location, and experience.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Internal AI Agent Infrastructure
jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over thousands of clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

​

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

​

Senior Software Engineer - Internal AI Agent Infrastructure

Why We Have This Role The Internal AI Agent Infrastructure team builds an internal cloud agent platform that helps Qualtrics engineers use AI agents running on company infrastructure. This role will contribute to the platform, including a near-term effort to support Press Ganey users with a different GitLab instance. The work also includes the MCP gateway, which connects approved tools and services for internal use. The platform helps engineers use AI capabilities while the team manages security and governance requirements. The role works with a senior engineering team and responds to feedback from engineers across Qualtrics.

How You'll Find Success

• Take initiative, be a self-starter, and propose ideas to move the team forward.

• Follow the latest industry trend changes in AI tooling and research how they could be applied to the platform.

• Possessing deep knowledge of agent concepts such as MCPs, skills, harnesses, and more.

• Advocate for changes that can improve platform usage, speed, or reliability.

• Use feedback from engineers to help shape platform work.

• Take responsibility for features through release and follow-up bug fixes.

How You'll Grow

• Develop experience building and maintaining an internal cloud agent platform.

• Learn about AI tools and developments by evaluating how they can be used at Qualtrics.

• Understand how to build and maintain security controls and provide AI governance to an enterprise.

• Hone your product management skills by learning the needs of our engineers to build out roadmaps boosting their productivity.

Things You'll Do

• Improve the platform by designing and implementing new features based on engineering needs and feedback.

• Expand access to the platform by supporting new GitLab instances and other repositories.

• Enable internal tool use by managing and governing our MCP Gateway which controls all MCP integrations.

• Partner with our security team to ensure all new toolings are compliant and adequate admin controls are in place.

• Proactively improve platform use and reliability by identifying bottlenecks and making changes to address them.

• Own delivered features through release and address bugs and technical debt that arise.

What We're Looking For On Your Resume

• Experience improving developer experience (DevEx), such as building, buying, or integrating tools for internal engineering teams.

• Hands-on expertise with modern AI tooling, including MCP servers, agent skills, agent harnesses, and using AI agents in your daily workflow.

• A track record of designing and building platforms that scale, along with reliable, maintainable systems and processes.

• Experience partnering directly with internal users to gather feedback, measure adoption, and turn pain points into product improvements.

• Strong ownership and communication skills, including driving cross-team initiatives, writing clear technical documentation, and helping other engineers adopt new tools and practices.

• Machine learning experience is a plus, not a requirement.

• 5+ years of software development experience.

What You Should Know About This Team

• The team has 6 people, all at senior level or above, and has an on-call rotation.

• Work is mostly focused coding, with a daily standup and usually about one weekly team discussion or design review.

• The team moves fast; we have at least one notable change each week that impacts all of engineering.

• The team uses feedback from engineers to guide platform improvements.

• The team's work includes reviewing new AI developments and considering how to make them usable by other engineers.

Our Team's Favorite Perks and Benefits

• Fun and collaborative office environment with in office amenities, food, drinks, outdoor space, and of course, pinball!

• Quarterly team offsites, giving developers a chance to interact with each other outside of the office and build camaraderie.

• Education budget you can flexibly spend on topics that interest you.

• QED (Qualtrics Engineer Development) Program encourages all engineers to invest in themselves up to 10% of their time each quarter to advance their careers.

The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life.

Qualtrics is an equal opportunity employer meaning that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

​​​​​​​Applicants in the United States of America have rights under Federal Employment Laws:Family & Medical Leave Act,Equal Opportunity Employment,Employee Polygraph Protection Act

Qualtrics is committed to the inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Qualtrics will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please let your Qualtrics contact/recruiter know.

Not finding a role that’s the right fit for now? Qualtrics Insiders is the one-stop shop for all things Qualtrics Life. Sign up for exclusive access to content created with you in mind and get the scoop on what we have going on at Qualtrics - upcoming events, behind the scenes stories from the team, interview tips, hot jobs, and more. No spam - we promise! You'll hear from us two times a month max with fresh, totally tailored info - so be sure to stay connected as you explore your best role and company fit.

​

A sign-on bonus and restricted stock units may be included in an employment offer. jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Site Reliability Engineer to join our Ground Software team. As a Site Reliability Engineer, you will design, build, and operate the ground and site network infrastructure that connects Apex facilities and mission operations across both commercial and secured environments. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who is equally comfortable architecting a highly available Kubernetes platform, and defining the security posture that keeps it all compliant. You will be a primary technical owner, setting the standards that the rest of the team builds on.




RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 - Architect and build ground and site network infrastructure spanning commercial and secured or classified environments through the platform layer.

 - Design, deploy, and scale highly available Kubernetes clusters that support workloads across multiple security and classification levels.

 - Own the security posture of ground infrastructure, defining and enforcing controls, hardening, and compliance for sensitive government and commercial programs.

 - Build and maintain infrastructure as code using Terraform, Terragrunt, and similar tooling so that environments are repeatable, reviewable, and fast to stand up.

 - Establish observability across the ground network, including monitoring, metrics, logging, and alerting, so issues are caught before they reach a mission.

 - Design and run CI/CD pipelines and automation that streamline deployments and reduce manual, error-prone work.

 - Act as a primary site reliability engineer for ground systems, driving uptime, incident response, and reliability standards on programs where downtime is not an option.

 - Partner with security, mission operations, and program teams to translate requirements into infrastructure that is both compliant and operable.

 - Set architectural standards and mentor other engineers, raising the bar for how ground infrastructure is built at Apex.


REQUIREMENTS:

 - Applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by U.S. export-control law.

 - 5+ years of experience in site reliability, infrastructure, or network engineering, with a meaningful portion in aerospace, defense, satellite, or another mission-critical domain.

 - Hands-on experience architecting and operating ground network or large-scale production network infrastructure.

 - Deep expertise with Kubernetes and containers, including building and scaling high availability clusters in production.

 - Strong networking fundamentals across routing, switching, segmentation, and secure network design.

 - Proven experience with infrastructure as code with CI/CD, automation, and observability tooling such as Prometheus, Grafana, or similar.

 - Working knowledge of security and compliance for regulated or classified environments, and the judgment to design a defensible security posture.

 - Proficiency scripting and building tooling in Python, Go, or a comparable language.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Active Top Secret or Top Secret/SCI clearance 

 - Prior experience supporting classified or government space programs or standing up infrastructure across multiple classification levels.

 - Familiarity with GitOps workflows and tools such as ArgoCD, and with modern observability stacks including Mimir.




#LI-AB1


WHY JOIN APEX?

Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one.




WHAT WE OFFER FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES:

 - Shared upside: Receive equity in Apex, letting you benefit from the work you create

 - Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for you and your dependents, plus $100k life insurance at no cost

 - Comprehensive PTO package:  Starting at 15 days vacation, growing to 20+ days annually, plus 10 paid holidays

 - Competitive 401(k) plan: Generous matching - 100% match on first 3%, 50% on next 2%

 - 8 weeks paid parental leave: Plus childcare reimbursement up to $350/day for work-related travel

 - Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks: To keep you fueled throughout the day

 - Vibrant community: Monthly office socials, pickleball tournaments, run club, and gatherings for you and your family

 - Your dream desk setup: All the tools you need to be your most productive self

 - World-class Playa Vista office: With the benefit of in-person collaboration with amazing coworkers and flexibility to integrate work and life

 - Real impact opportunity: Work alongside experts from aerospace, new space, and other cutting-edge industries to make a lasting difference




ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: 

Compensation ranges are set by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. A candidate's specific level and base pay are determined case by case and may vary with job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities, and internal equity. Beyond base salary, full-time hires are also eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options, along with medical, dental, and vision coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

Apex's work is governed by U.S. export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). To be eligible for this role, applicants must either (1) qualify as a U.S. Person, meaning a U.S. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident (green card holder), a refugee admitted under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or an individual granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or (2) be able to obtain the required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State, the U.S. Department of Commerce, or another applicable U.S. government agency. You can learn more about ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Fundamentals Visiting Professor
jobs.description:
Opportunity at a Glance

Do you remember the professor who encouraged you to believe in yourself and in your ability to be the successful nurse professional you are today?  Now you have the unique opportunity to be that professor  and create the "a-ha" moment of sudden insight and comprehension that will change a nursing student's life forever. As a Part-Time Visiting Professor, you will inspire our motivated students to realize their educational and career goals while enjoying a flexible schedule, excellent compensation, strong mentorship and support programs, plus significant opportunities for career growth. From individual professor support and student-led study groups to diverse clinical and career networking opportunities, the institution's community shares a common goal: to give each other the care we need to succeed and make a difference by transforming healthcare.   If you are passionate about nursing and advancing your career through the power of education, we want to talk with you today.

Fundamental Nursing Skills- Content focuses on health promotion and the rehabilitative aspects of patient care. Students provide direct patient care in the acquisition of skills and concepts of professional nursing. The nursing process is utilized as the student implements basic aspects of nursing practice.

Responsibilities

• Implements the College's philosophy, curriculum, program outcomes, and course objectives through clinical teaching, and service to the College, community, health system and profession.

• Assumes responsibility for all autonomous aspects of individual teaching loads.

• Plans clinical experiences for and provides direct supervision and evaluation of nursing students delivering nursing care to an individual or group of individuals.

• Makes self-available to staff at the agencies.

• Evaluates and provides documented feedback to student on level of performance based on course objectives.

• Is available for remediation of students as required or needed.

• Orients and maintains current knowledge related to agency/clinical policies, procedures, and expectations with the assistance of the agency/clinical personnel.

• Develops and posts written clinical assignments consistent with student's knowledge base, skill competency and individual learning needs.

• Corrects and returns homework, quizzes, tests, lab assignments, clinical paperwork and other written work in a timely manner.

jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila is hiring a Director of Lab Platform Engineering to lead the team that builds and operates the hybrid on-premises and cloud infrastructure behind our automated labs. You will own the platform strategy for a fleet of distributed lab sites and lead the engineers who make new sites come online reliably and repeatably.

Lab Platform Engineering builds and supports the platforms and software that keep Lila's AI Science Factory™ running: bare metal clusters, cloud infrastructure, secure identity and secrets services, resilient storage, and the APIs and tooling that let scientists and engineers ship software to production. Every robot, instrument, and lab workflow depends on these systems.

This is a leadership role on a team being built now. You will grow the organization to 10 to 15 engineers, set multi-year technical direction, and partner with robotics, lab operations, research, and security leaders on what the platform needs to support next.

What You'll Be Building

• Build and lead a team of 10 to 15 engineers, including managers and tech leads. Hire, develop, and retain engineers at every level.

• Set multi-year technical vision and strategy for hybrid edge and cloud infrastructure across distributed lab sites.

• Own platform roadmap and delivery, shipping on a predictable cadence against commitments made to partner teams.

• Own fleet operations and reliability, including service levels, on-call, and incident response across sites.

• Own infrastructure budget, capacity planning, and vendor relationships.

• Partner cross-functionally with robotics, lab operations, research, and security, and communicate platform strategy and tradeoffs to executives.

• Raise the engineering bar through standards, review practices, and technical thought leadership.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• 15+ years in software or infrastructure engineering, with 8+ years leading teams, including managing managers or tech leads, or equivalent practical experience.

• Track record building and scaling a platform or infrastructure organization from a small team upward.

• Deep technical grounding in hybrid on-premises and cloud infrastructure, including Kubernetes operated at scale outside the public cloud.

• Experience operating production fleets against explicit reliability targets, with ownership of on-call and incident practice.

• Ownership of infrastructure budget, capacity planning, and vendor negotiation.

• Proven cross-functional and executive partnership, including communicating technical tradeoffs to non-engineering leaders.

• Demonstrated ability to hire and develop senior and principal-level engineers.

Bonus Points For

• Scientific domain: laboratory automation, robotics, or hardware-adjacent platforms; lab software for life sciences or materials science.

• Distributed and edge systems: multi-site operations, intermittently connected environments, over-the-air software rollout.

• Security and compliance: identity and secrets management across hybrid environments, operating in regulated or audited settings.

• Platform practice: infrastructure-as-code, GitOps, developer experience as a product, AI-assisted engineering workflows adopted across a team.

• Organizational: standing up a new function, integrating acquired or transferred teams, managing a team split across offices and remote.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

Expected Base Salary Range

$232,000—$390,000 USD

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Systems Engineering Intern - Safety Analysis (Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Systems Engineering Intern - Safety Analysis on our Systems Engineering team, you'll help push forward the analysis that gives REGENT confidence in the safety of the Seaglider as we work toward certification. You'll support development of a safety analysis method we don't yet perform in-house and support ongoing safety analysis efforts already underway. Beyond safety analysis, you'll get hands-on exposure to the broader systems engineering discipline, lending support on requirements management, verification, and the systems engineering work behind our hybridization efforts.

This isn't a role where you'll be handed a checklist and told exactly what to do each day. You'll scope your own path to completion on a defined project, work directly with engineers across multiple disciplines to understand how your analysis connects to the bigger picture, and carry your work through to an internal engineering approval process by the end of your term - a level of real ownership that's rare for an internship. 

Seagliders are a genuinely new kind of vehicle, and the certification path we're building for them is just as novel, which means the questions you'll help answer haven't been answered by anyone else before. If you're the kind of person who gets energized by ambiguity, asks questions instead of waiting for direction, and wants a front-row seat to how safety-critical systems actually get certified, we'd love to have you on the team.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Support Development of a New Safety Analysis: You'll lead a safety analysis method REGENT hasn't yet brought in-house, such as a PRA, ZHA, or CMA, and help establish how we approach it going forward.

 - Strengthen Requirements and Verification: You'll provide systems engineering support across requirements management and verification, helping ensure our design decisions are traceable and well-documented.

 - Support Hybridization Efforts: You'll contribute systems engineering work to our hybridization systems, getting exposure to how power and propulsion decisions ripple across the broader vehicle design.

 - Scope Your Own Project: You'll define your own path to completion on a defined project, deciding how to break down the work and what questions need answering along the way.

 - Work Across Disciplines: You'll collaborate closely with engineers from different technical backgrounds, learning how safety analysis connects to the decisions being made across the vehicle.

 - Present Your Work for Approval: By the end of your term, you'll present your results to the broader engineering organization and carry your analysis through an actual internal approval process.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Clear Technical Communication: You're comfortable explaining your thinking to people across teams, including delivering technical updates to engineering leadership.

 - A Grounding in One Discipline: You have a solid understanding of at least one engineering discipline, which gives you a strong base for quickly picking up the new concepts this role will throw at you.

 - Systems Thinking: Any exposure to systems engineering principles will help you ramp up faster and see how your piece of the project fits into the larger whole.

 - Passion for Being on the Water or in the Air: You're excited by aviation, sailing, boating, or anything that gets you out on the water or into the sky. Whether you're an experienced pilot, an avid boater, or simply fascinated by how things fly and move through water, that curiosity and enthusiasm are what matter most. Hands-on experience is a bonus!

 - Safety Analysis Familiarity: Any background in system safety or Root Cause Analysis principles will help you get up to speed more quickly on the work ahead.

 - Comfort With Python or MATLAB: Experience with either opens you up to a wider range of tasks and analysis approaches during your term.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Applied AI
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

At Pika, we're looking for a technically strong, client-facing AI researcher who can turn customer feedback into models and workflows that solve real business needs. You'll work directly with clients to understand what they want to achieve, identify where current model outputs fall short, and fine-tune or post-train models for their use cases. When the solution calls for more than model adaptation, you'll build the supporting workflow.

This is a full-time, hands-on, revenue-driven applied research role. Clear communication, professional client service, reliable delivery, and independent execution matter as much as technical ability. You'll help clients get value quickly, build their confidence in working with Pika, and help turn successful technical work into closed engagements and ongoing business.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Understand the client's needs. Listen carefully, ask focused questions, and translate requests and feedback into a clear problem, practical scope, and agreed success criteria.

 - Adapt models for real use cases. Fine-tune and post-train models to address client needs. Prepare relevant examples and evaluation criteria, diagnose gaps, and verify that each iteration improves the outcomes the client cares about.

 - Build the complete solution. Create or adapt workflows around models when needed, connecting APIs, tools, and processing steps into a usable solution that fits the client's deployment needs.

 - Iterate quickly with clients. Share working results early, gather specific feedback, and make focused improvements in short cycles. Balance quality, complexity, cost, and delivery speed to keep projects moving.

 - Communicate professionally. Explain technical options and limitations clearly, set realistic expectations, respond thoughtfully to requests, and keep clients informed about progress and next steps. Build a relationship that makes them want to continue working with Pika.

 - Own execution and coordinate with the team. Drive day-to-day work with independence while keeping teammates aligned on requirements, priorities, progress, and blockers. Ask for input or escalate risks early when needed.

 - Deliver for deployment. Help move successful experiments into usable deployments, with clear evaluation results, reproducible workflows, and the documentation needed for handoff.

 - Help close client engagements. Demonstrate the solution's value, address technical concerns, and work with the team to turn successful iterations into client commitments and revenue.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience fine-tuning or post-training generative AI models, with the ability to diagnose model behavior and evaluate whether an adaptation solves the intended problem.

 - Strong coding and practical ML skills: you can implement experiments, work with data, debug model pipelines, and build supporting workflows.

 - Excellent listening and communication skills. You can understand an ambiguous request, clarify what matters, and explain technical work to clients with different levels of expertise.

 - Professional judgment, reliability, and a service mindset. You handle feedback constructively, communicate limitations honestly, take ownership of commitments, and build trust through consistent follow-through.

 - Independence and ownership, combined with strong communication and collaboration within the team.

 - The ability to work in fast feedback cycles, prioritize the highest-impact improvements, and connect technical decisions to client value and commercial outcomes.



PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - Prior professional experience in a similar client-facing AI or ML role, with end-to-end delivery from requirements and model adaptation through evaluation, integration, and deployment. This experience is strongly preferred.

 - Delivering reliable AI solutions for external clients or users and supporting them through feedback and iteration.

 - LoRA fine-tuning, other parameter-efficient adaptation methods, or feedback-driven post-training.

 - Building model evaluation pipelines, API integrations, or workflows used in a deployed product.

 - Participating in customer demos, technical pilots, or the delivery of paid projects.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Success is measured by how well you serve clients, how quickly you turn feedback into useful improvements, and how reliably your work meets their deployment needs. Strong performance builds client trust, helps close engagements, encourages continued collaboration, and contributes to revenue.

jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Creative Experiences
jobs.description:
Open to full-time hires and interns.



ABOUT THE ROLE

At Pika, we're looking for a creative, hands-on AI researcher who can turn the latest models, APIs, and emerging ideas into compelling experiences people want to try and share. You'll combine models across image, video, audio, and language to build workflows, demos, and features that bring people to Pika and contribute to revenue growth.

This is a goal-driven applied research role, open to both full-time hires and interns. You'll take ideas from an initial opportunity through experimentation, implementation, and delivery, then use feedback and results to decide what to improve next. Strong creative judgment, resourcefulness, and fast execution are central to the role.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Find promising opportunities. Stay close to new models, tools, creative formats, and cultural trends. Identify ideas with a clear audience, use case, and potential to drive interest, website traffic, or revenue.

 - Build end to end. Combine existing models, APIs, and tools into working multimodal workflows. Own the path from a rough concept to a usable demo, creative asset, or product experience.

 - Choose the right amount of research. Test practical approaches quickly. Use lightweight LoRA fine-tuning or targeted post-training when it meaningfully improves the result and fits the project's time budget.

 - Deliver frequently. Work in short iteration cycles, set a clear scope for each experiment, and get strong first versions out quickly. Make thoughtful trade-offs between additional research, output quality, cost, and time to delivery.

 - Create work ready to share. Produce compelling demos and creative outputs that the team can use for social media, launches, and other growth efforts. Personally posting on or managing social channels is not required.

 - Learn from results. Use audience response, product feedback, and relevant traffic or revenue signals to decide which ideas to refine, expand, or stop.

 - Make successful work reusable. Leave working workflows, examples, and concise documentation so the team can reproduce and build on what you deliver.
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience building with generative AI models, APIs, or creative workflows, with examples of work you have taken from idea to a working result.

 - Strong prototyping and coding skills: you can connect tools, debug a pipeline, and make an end-to-end experience work.

 - A creative, entrepreneurial mindset and good judgment about what makes an output compelling, useful, and worth sharing. You enjoy the pace and resourcefulness of a hackathon: testing ideas quickly and getting a working result into people's hands.

 - Curiosity across modalities and the ability to learn unfamiliar models and tools quickly.

 - Ownership and comfort with tight timelines: you can prioritize, simplify an approach, and recognize when shipping and learning is more valuable than further polishing.

 - A clear connection between technical choices and the intended user or business outcome.
   


HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

 - Experience as a startup founder or early-stage startup team member, or actively building and testing startup ideas.

 - Hackathon wins or standout hackathon projects that demonstrate rapid prototyping, resourcefulness, and end-to-end execution.

 - LoRA fine-tuning, lightweight model adaptation, or other targeted post-training.

 - Combining image, video, audio, or language models in a single workflow.

 - Building creative demos, interactive prototypes, or AI experiences that reached real users.
   


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

You deliver a steady stream of compelling, usable experiments; turn the strongest ideas into repeatable workflows; and use each release to learn what attracts users and contributes to Pika's growth. Success depends on the quality, speed, and impact of what you deliver.

jobs.title: Engineering Intern to the Chief Engineer (Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT is looking for an Engineering Intern to work with the Chief Engineer - Viceroy, spending a summer at the center of Viceroy, our first manned certification program, working directly alongside the person responsible for how it all comes together. This isn't an internship built around one discipline or one team. You'll move across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software work as the program demands it, picking up analysis, drawings, and integration tasks wherever the need is greatest during an intense and fast-moving stretch of the program. It's a rare chance to see how a complex vehicle program actually fits together end to end, rather than experiencing just one slice of it.

You'll sit within our Engineering & Technology team and report directly to the Chief Engineer, who will actively coach and mentor you through the breadth of the role rather than narrowing it down to something more conventional. Because this is a newly created position, you'll have real input into shaping what it becomes, including helping define what a technically grounded systems engineering path looks like at REGENT going forward. If you're the kind of person who gets energized by variety, wants to understand how mechanical, electrical, controls, and software decisions interact to shape a vehicle's performance, cost, and schedule, and is excited by the idea of helping bring Seagliders into reality from the inside, this is a role where you'll thrive.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Float Across the Program: You'll move across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software work on Viceroy, going wherever the program needs help most on a given week.

 - Dig Into Analysis and Drawings: You'll contribute to the analysis and drawing work driving Viceroy forward during a particularly active stretch of the program.

 - Lead a Cross-Discipline Trade Study: By the midpoint of the term, you'll complete a trade study that touches multiple disciplines from start to finish, building a real understanding of how system-level decisions affect performance, cost, and schedule.

 - Build Toward Integration: You'll work toward getting an integrated subsystem running in our hardware-in-the-loop environment by the end of the term, whether that's a VCC controlling an actuator or a sensor-fused solution providing feedback.

 - Learn Directly From the Chief Engineer: You'll get hands-on coaching and mentorship as you navigate the breadth of the role, with someone invested in helping you connect the dots across disciplines.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Multidisciplinary Technical Grounding: You have real experience or coursework in systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, or software engineering, and ideally more than one of these.

 - Mechatronics Curiosity: Exposure to mechanisms or electromechanical systems is a plus and will help you move comfortably between disciplines.

 - Genuine Enthusiasm for Seagliders: You're drawn to the idea of reinventing coastal transportation and want to understand how a real vehicle program comes together.

 - Comfort With Ambiguity: You're energized rather than overwhelmed by a role without a fixed lane, and you're ready to shape your own path alongside your manager.

 - Clear, Confident Communication: You can communicate well across teams and disciplines, translating what you're learning into useful updates and questions.

 - A Strong Appetite to Learn: You're ready to be taught almost everything, and you bring the curiosity and follow-through to make the most of that.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.
